config.title: Build todo CRUD REST API

intro.title: Build todo CRUD REST API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a todo CRUD REST API using Node.js. You will learn how to create, read, update, and delete todo items through HTTP endpoints. The core programming concepts involve handling HTTP requests, managing data in memory, and structuring a simple server with routes. You'll use key Node.js constructs like the built-in 'http' module and basic JavaScript objects to implement the API logic.
intro.usecase: This pattern is the foundation of countless interactive web and mobile applications. For example, any task management app like Asana or Todoist uses a todo CRUD API to let users create, view, update, and delete their tasks, syncing these changes across all devices. As a developer, you'll implement similar APIs for features like user profiles in social apps, product listings in e-commerce backends, or content management in publishing tools, where persistent data operations are essential.

objectives: Initialize a Node.js project with Express framework and required dependencies
Configure Express middleware to handle JSON requests and CORS
Implement a data structure to store todo items in memory
Construct REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting todo items
Apply proper HTTP status codes and response formats for each CRUD operation
Integrate request validation to ensure data integrity for todo operations
Manipulate the in-memory data store through each CRUD endpoint
Control API behavior by handling edge cases and error scenarios

steps.title: Import Express and create Express app
steps.instruction: Import Express using require() and create an Express application instance. Store the app instance in a constant variable named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use require('express') to import Express, then call express() to create the app instance.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express and create the app instance here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the Express module imported and an app instance ready for configuration.
successCriteria: Express is imported using require() and an Express application instance is created and stored in a variable named 'app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using require('express') and storing the result of express() in a variable named 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import Express and create the app instance.

steps.title: Add middleware for JSON parsing
steps.instruction: Add the express.json() middleware to your Express app so it can parse incoming JSON request bodies.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with express.json() as the argument to add the JSON parsing middleware.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will be configured to automatically parse JSON data from incoming requests.
successCriteria: The app.use(express.json()) middleware is added to your Express application.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using app.use() with express.json() as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The JSON parsing middleware isn't properly configured. Remember to use app.use(express.json()) to add the middleware.

steps.title: Initialize in-memory todos array
steps.instruction: Create an array variable named 'todos' to store todo objects, with each object having 'id', 'title', and 'completed' properties. Initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: Declare a variable using 'const' or 'let' and assign it an empty array. You can add placeholder todo objects later.
steps.expectedOutcome: A variable named 'todos' is declared and initialized as an empty array, ready to store todo objects.
successCriteria: The code contains a variable declaration for 'todos' that is an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared a variable named 'todos' and initialized it as an empty array ([]).
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a variable called 'todos' and set it to an empty array. This will serve as our temporary database for todo items.

steps.title: Create GET /todos endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a GET route handler at '/todos' that returns the entire todos array as JSON.
steps.hint: Use app.get() to define the route. The handler function should take request and response parameters, then call res.json() with the todos array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET endpoint at '/todos' that returns the todos array in JSON format.
successCriteria: The route handler is defined with app.get('/todos', handler) and returns todos using res.json(todos).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.get() with '/todos' and returning the todos array with res.json().
steps.feedbackWrong: The GET endpoint isn't set up correctly. Review how to define routes with Express.

steps.title: Create POST /todos endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a POST route handler for '/todos' that adds a new todo object to the todos array. The handler should read the todo data from the request body and assign it a unique id.
steps.hint: Use app.post() to define the route. Inside the handler, create a new todo object with properties from req.body and push it to the todos array. Remember to send a response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST endpoint at '/todos' is created that successfully adds new todo objects to the todos array and returns the created todo with a 201 status.
successCriteria: The POST endpoint is defined with app.post(), reads todo data from req.body, assigns a unique id, pushes the new todo to the todos array, and sends a response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your endpoint reads the todo data from the request body, assigns an id, and sends a proper response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint is not correctly implemented. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Add input validation for POST endpoint
steps.instruction: In the POST /todos endpoint, add a validation check to ensure the request body contains a 'title' property before creating a new todo.
steps.hint: Check if req.body.title exists. If it doesn't, send a 400 status with an error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST endpoint will now validate that the request body contains a title before creating a new todo.
successCriteria: The POST endpoint includes a validation check that returns a 400 status with an error message when title is missing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your validation returns a proper error response when title is missing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation check is missing or incorrect. The endpoint should check for req.body.title and return a 400 status if it's not present.

steps.title: Create GET /todos/:id endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a GET route handler that finds and returns a specific todo by ID from the URL parameter.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with '/todos/:id' path. Access the id parameter via req.params.id. Find the todo in the todos array using find() and return it with res.json(). If not found, return a 404 status.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET endpoint that retrieves a single todo by ID from the todos array.
successCriteria: The endpoint uses app.get() with '/todos/:id', finds the todo by ID, returns it as JSON if found, and returns a 404 status if not found.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to handle both cases: returning the todo if found and a 404 error if not found.
steps.feedbackWrong: The endpoint is missing or incorrect. Ensure you use app.get() with the correct path, find the todo by ID, and handle both success and error responses.

steps.title: Add error handling for GET /todos/:id
steps.instruction: Inside the GET /todos/:id endpoint, add logic to return a 404 status with a JSON error message when the requested todo ID doesn't exist in the todos array.
steps.hint: After finding the todo by ID, check if it exists. If not, use res.status(404).json() to send an error response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The endpoint will now properly handle invalid todo IDs by returning a 404 error response.
successCriteria: The GET /todos/:id endpoint includes a check for non-existent todos and returns a 404 status with a JSON error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check if the todo exists and return a 404 status with a JSON error message when it doesn't.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if the todo exists after finding it by ID, and return a 404 status with a JSON error message when it doesn't exist.

steps.title: Create PUT /todos/:id endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a PUT route handler for '/todos/:id' that updates a specific todo's properties.
steps.hint: Use app.put() with the route path and a callback that receives req and res. Inside, find the todo by id from req.params, update its properties from req.body, and send the updated todo as JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PUT route handler is added that can update an existing todo by id.
successCriteria: The code includes app.put('/todos/:id', ...) with logic to find the todo by id, update its properties, and respond with the updated todo.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the PUT endpoint, but make sure it finds the todo by id, updates its properties, and sends the updated todo as JSON.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PUT endpoint is missing or incomplete. Check the route path, the callback function, and the update logic.

steps.title: Create DELETE /todos/:id endpoint
steps.instruction: Create a DELETE route handler for '/todos/:id' that removes a specific todo from the todos array.
steps.hint: Use app.delete() with a route parameter to find the todo by id and remove it from the array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DELETE endpoint is added that can remove todos by their id.
successCriteria: The DELETE endpoint is defined with app.delete(), finds the todo by id, removes it from the array, and returns appropriate responses.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your DELETE endpoint finds the todo by id, removes it from the array, and returns a proper response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DELETE endpoint is missing or incorrect. Review how to create a DELETE route and remove items from an array.

steps.title: Start the server on a port
steps.instruction: Add an app.listen() call at the end of your file to start the Express server on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use app.listen() with the port number and optionally a callback function that logs a message when the server starts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen on port 3000, making your API accessible via HTTP.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and optionally includes a callback that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your server is now configured to start on port 3000.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added app.listen(), but make sure it's on port 3000 and includes the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly configured to start. Check that you've added app.listen(3000, ...) at the end of your file.

steps.title: Add basic error handling middleware
steps.instruction: Add a generic error handling middleware function after all your route handlers to catch and respond to any unhandled errors.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with four parameters: (err, req, res, next). Inside, send a 500 status with a JSON error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your API will now have a fallback error handler that catches any unhandled errors and returns a consistent 500 error response.
successCriteria: An error handling middleware function is added using app.use() with four parameters, logs the error, and sends a 500 status with a JSON error response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your middleware has all four parameters (err, req, res, next) and sends a proper JSON response with status 500.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling middleware is missing or incomplete. Remember to use app.use() with four parameters to catch errors, and send a 500 status with a JSON error message.
